items.title: Why "Brought Dead" Is the Default Fate in Indian Hospitals | Dr. Srikanth K.N.
items.description: Orthopaedic surgeon Dr. Srikanth K.N. (FRCS) explains why Indian hospitals increasingly declare arriving patients dead on arrival by default. It isn't incompetence. After years of doctors being assaulted and hospitals vandalized when a resuscitation attempt fails, the safest clinical decision became not trying at all. From the full conversation on redesigning Indian healthcare from scratch, on The Idea Sandbox.

items.title: India's Emergency Response is Broken. Here's How AI Fixes It.
items.description:
Every year, India loses 2.4 million people to treatable conditions — heart attacks, road accidents, snakebites, maternal emergencies.

The treatments exist. The hospitals exist. The ambulances exist.

What's missing is coordination.

Only 7% of trauma patients in India reach a hospital within the "Golden Hour" — that critical 60-minute window when intervention saves lives. In the US, it's over 50%.

India’s stray dog crisis is usually framed as “cruel owners” vs “dangerous dogs” but what if the real story is poverty, fear and caste.

items.title: Why Artists Hate Their Own Work (And Why That’s Okay)
items.description:
If you make anything - paintings, photos, podcasts - you probably hate your own work the moment it’s finished, then cringe at it years later.
